component.name: bava
component.summary: Music visualizer driven by cavacore and MPRIS

description.p: bava is a Linux music visualizer built on the Bevy engine. It captures the default audio output's monitor natively through PipeWire (falling back to PulseAudio), runs it through cavacore — the analysis engine from CAVA — and renders smoothed, log-spaced frequency bars with HDR bloom.
It also reads now-playing metadata over MPRIS, showing the current track's title, artist, and album, and fetching album art into a dimmed backdrop when the player exposes it.

ul.li: Real-time spectrum analysis with configurable bars, smoothing, and frequency range
Eleven Cavalier-style drawing modes (bars, wave, particles, circles, and more)
Physics mode: rigid bodies that collide with the live spectrum
Now-playing track info and album art over MPRIS
Colors extracted from the current track's album art
In-app settings editor with live-reflected changes and named profiles
Offline music-video rendering of an audio file to MP4

screenshot.caption: Frequency bars reacting to playing audio

description.p: Resting orb contacts, configurable cover linger, retrying audio capture and album-art downloads, and safer config saves.
Puffin profiling, batched per-frame meshes and scoped ball CCD for higher ball counts, and a browser build of the same visualizer.
Eleven Cavalier-style drawing modes, avian2d physics mode, dynamic album-art colors, and offline video rendering.
Initial Flatpak release: bars/monstercat visualizer, MPRIS now-playing with album art, and the in-app settings editor.
